management.value: Management/Board Magda Chambriard (born 1957) became Petrobras CEO in May 2024, the second woman to ever lead the company. She is notably the sixth CEO in five years, a reflection of Brazil's political volatility around the company. Her background: Civil Engineering degree from UFRJ (1979); Master's in Chemical Engineering (1989). Started her career at Petrobras in 1980 in oil production/reservoir engineering — spent 22 years there. From 2012–2016, served as Director-General of Brazil's National Petroleum Agency (ANP) — the oil industry regulator — under President Dilma Rousseff. After leaving ANP, worked as an energy consultant. Was part of President Lula's transition team after his 2022 election She is a genuine petroleum engineer with deep technical credentials and industry relationships. However, she is a Lula political appointee, which colors her strategic priorities (more domestic investment, reinstatement of fertilizer plants, Amazon exploration). She received a contract extension through April 2027. During her time at ANP, she faced criticism over potential conflicts of interest and her role during the OGX bankruptcy saga. These did not prevent her appointment. Her turnaround plan includes: aggressive pre-salt production growth, reviving refineries and fertilizer plants, Amazon frontier drilling, and net-zero carbon by 2050.
